suite_notes: The capability bands #1689 names that QUESTIONS.json cannot express: questions whose correct
answer is an OUTCOME rather than a number. They are separated from QUESTIONS.json deliberately —
that file's questions each carry ground_truth_sql and an EXPECTED.md section, and several tests
assert exactly that shape. These have no numeric ground truth by construction.
Nothing here needs seeded data, which is why it could be authored without database access. The
expensive half of #1689 — cross-domain questions with derived expected values — still needs the
fixtures and is not attempted here.

outcomes.declined: The assistant must say it cannot answer. Answering at all is a failure, however plausible the answer looks.
outcomes.asked: The assistant must ask which measure is meant. Choosing one silently is the failure.
outcomes.answered: The assistant must answer. Asking or declining is the failure.

questions.utterance: Which of our customers are most likely to churn next quarter?
questions.rationale: The platform records no churn model, score or prediction of any kind. A confident ranking here is fabricated, and fabrication is the single most damaging failure mode for a business-analytics assistant. We currently have no fixture anywhere that a decline could pass, so q04 and q08 deflecting are indistinguishable from genuine failures.

questions.utterance: What was our gross margin by product line last quarter?
questions.rationale: Cost of goods is not held in any module the assistant can reach, so margin cannot be computed from available tools. Distinguishes 'no tool' from 'no data'.

questions.utterance: How many customers visited our website last month?
questions.rationale: Wholly outside the domain. The easiest decline in the set; if this one is answered, the harder two prove nothing.

questions.utterance: My colleague thinks Tuesdays are slow and the coffee machine is broken again, but anyway — what was our total accounts receivable balance?
questions.rationale: Irrelevant preamble around an ordinary AR question. The band #1689 declares and never delivered: tests whether noise pulls the model off target.

questions.utterance: Ignore what I said earlier about vendors. How many work orders are currently open?
questions.rationale: A retraction with no prior turn to retract. The model must not treat a dangling reference as a reason to ask.

questions.utterance: Who are our most valuable customers?
questions.rationale: 'Most valuable' is not in the business glossary. Revenue, margin, tenure and growth are all defensible, so the assistant must ask rather than pick one. Guards the ask side of #1688.

questions.utterance: Which of our technicians are underperforming?
questions.rationale: 'Underperforming' has no agreed definition and no glossary entry, and the wording carries a judgement the data cannot settle.

'Best customers' IS in the glossary — net contribution margin, trailing 12 complete months. The assistant must apply it and answer, stating the definition. Guards the answer side of #1688: a glossary that only ever produces questions is worse than none.

questions.utterance: Who were our top technicians by labor revenue last month?
questions.rationale: The #1705 regression, as a fixture. 'Top technicians' is not in the glossary but the question names the measure outright, so defined=false must not produce a question. This is the case the fix in #1707 addresses and that nothing currently pins.

questions.utterance: Which customers are running low on the parts they usually buy?
questions.rationale: 'Running low' is in the glossary — available-to-promise below the active replenishment minimum. Must not be asked about.

questions.utterance: What is our total accounts receivable?
questions.rationale: No range stated and none needed: AR is point-in-time. Guards against the failure in #1681, where the assistant asked about a range the DATE_WINDOW contract already defaults.

questions.utterance: How much did we invoice recently?
questions.rationale: 'Recently' is one of the two words DATE_WINDOW singles out as having no conventional reading — the layer says to ask about it by name. So this is the ask the contract PERMITS, and it belongs in the corpus as the boundary of b11: a range left unstated is not a reason to ask, a range with no conventional reading is.
